mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever felt like if you can’t do something perfectly, maybe it’s just not worth doing at all? You’re definitely not alone there. Perfectionism is sneaky—it quietly convinces us that if our work isn’t flawless, we might as well not bother. But what if there’s a different way? In Jon Acuff’s book, Finish: Give Yourself the Gift of Done, we’re invited to explore a new mindset—one that celebrates the simple, powerful act of finishing, instead of chasing the impossible standard of perfection. Think about it: starting something new always feels exciting, but actually seeing it through to the end? That’s where the real magic happens. Along the way, we all face obstacles—self-doubt, procrastination, maybe even a fear of not measuring up. Yet, it’s in those smaller, steady steps—the ones that move us closer to the finish line—where we find real growth and transformation. Together, we’re going to unpack why so many of us abandon our goals halfway and how shifting our focus from perfection to progress can make all the difference. Acuff offers practical strategies and a bit of humor to help us navigate setbacks, embrace our imperfections, and discover the true joy of actually getting things done. So, as we set off on this journey, let’s trade in the heavy weight of perfect for the lighter, more rewarding feeling of done. Are you ready to see what lasting change and satisfaction really look like? Let’s explore it together.
